chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Basie's relaxed swing versus Crawford's hard digging style
summary: Crawford contrasts his own pushing, digging approach with Basie's smooth natural swing and Jo Jones, and with Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well now, when you say there were things that you didn't understand in his band, what do you mean?

Well, I guess the gouging in, you know, digging in. Like I was used to hearing Lunsford all my life -- not all my life, but up until we formed the Lunsford outfit. And so I was just a natural digger, and I couldn't help it. I mean behind my drums and everything I had to dig in. That was my style and my taste.
People like Chick Webb, um-m, one of the world's greatest drummers.
When you say dig in, I mean -- you mean that --
Push, grab and play. I had to play hard. I was a hard player.
And so now, what do you see was the difference between the way you all were playing and the way Basie's band played?

Well, Basie was a smoothie, natural swinger. I mean a natural swinger. And so it took me a little while to get used to that because the man had great musicians in his band, and Jo Jones was there, and that little rascal, as I told you before, he revolutionized drums to me.
Chick Webb was still the greatest. That is the

trouble right today of the modern day drummer. They never had the chance to hear Chick Webb. To me he was the greatest, little hunchbacker from Baltimore, around there somewhere, and I just idolized the man.

Well now, you say -- excuse me. I wanted to try to get it a little clearer here. Now, when you say Basie's Kansas City band, things you didn't understand about it, you mean that they were -- they swung more relaxed? Is that what you're saying, and more relaxed swing.

Yeah, they were -- me, I was a pusher and a gouger. In other words, if I couldn't lift a band in whatever kind of beat I was playing, you know, if I couldn't dig in myself and lift that whole band, well, then I'd consider myself nothing. But I was just a hard worker.
